results.title: Descendant Community Engagement | UGA Archaeology
results.content: # Descendant Community Engagement. The Laboratory’s approach to community engagement is multilayered and includes shared stewardship, multi-vocal approaches, two-way communication, trust, capacity building, equitable partnerships, knowledge sharing, transparency, and joint decision-making. We refer to this as descendant community-informed institutional integrity (DCIII). By recognizing that the Lab houses collections that are the intellectual and cultural property of many different descendant communities, we have shifted to practices that include the active exchange of ideas and the development of mutual respect the centers on correcting past mistakes and views within archaeology. ### **What Is a Descendant Community?**. A "descendant community" within the Laboratory can mean many things, including, but not limited to, a tribal nation or an organization or family representing a diasporic or other community of origin. A descendant community retains ancestral and cultural ties to collections stewarded by the Laboratory. The Lab’s implementation of our mission, in practice, now centers on high integrity through deep collaboration where our descendant community partners and archaeologists are equal decision-makers. One way we have incorporated this is through the Lab's new policies and procedures that were revised with descendant community input, including **NAGPRA** policies and a revised **collections management policy**. We have also established advisory boards comprised of descendent community representatives, Laboratory directors, and university faculty. Through ongoing efforts in building relationships and trust, the Lab has established an “open-door” philosophy with descendent communities concerning projects and collections. Regular communication and transparency concerning our work at the Lab is essential to ensure descendent community representation in decision-making and cooperative planning. These partnerships have directly allowed for the integration of descendant community perspectives in all aspects of lab management and policies, including research access, education and public engagement, and curation and collections management. Through collaboration, we can foster a community of university-wide institutional integrity with respect for descendent communities and their histories. Descendant community engagement has enhanced our ability to be a more conscientious organization that centers on people and their histories, not merely the objects of scientific study. Our journey is ongoing, and we hope that the Lab will always retain this evolving and multivocal flow regarding the input of Indigenous and other descendant community perspectives and knowledge.

results.title: Community Engagement Manager - Cardano constitution consultation | Intersect - Knowledge Base
results.content: # Community Engagement Manager - Cardano constitution consultation. Intersect and its members play an important role in shaping the proposed on-chain governance mechanisms - and the development of off-chain tools and processes to support it, including the rollout of Cardano’s first Constitution. During 2024, the drafting process and ratification of Cardano’s Constitution will take place, involving thousands of participants across the world. We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Community Engagement Manager to join our team on a nine month full-time contract. During this important period of growth and development for the Cardano ecosystem, this role will be pivotal in supporting the consultation period for Cardano's constitution - a foundational activity that will shape the future of the network for all ada holders. As the Community Engagement Manager, you will lead our efforts to ensure broad and meaningful participation from the Cardano community during the consultation process. This role will act as the point of contact for the Constitution workshop hosts and convention delegates to provide prompt, accurate and supportive information so they can confidently participate. In addition, through social media and community spaces, you will nurture key relationships, support the Civics Committee within Intersect, and support the Intersect community & communication teams more broadly to promote inclusion and accessibility throughout the Cardano ecosystem during the consultation process. * Develop and implement comprehensive community engagement strategies to drive meaningful conversations around the topic of governance that inform and empower the Cardano community . * Ensure workshop hosts and delegates are properly supported, elevating their experience participating with the Cardano Constitution. * Manage social media platforms and other communication channels to help disseminate information, drive conversations and gather feedback across the community. * Monitor and report on community sentiment and feedback, providing insights to the project team to help guide consensual and collaborative development of the constitution. * Strong understanding and awareness of Cardano's technology, ecosystem, and community. * Be part of a passionate and innovative team supporting the community rolling out Cardano’s groundbreaking governance features. * Opportunity to play a key supporting role in shaping the future of Cardano. If you are passionate about Cardano, blockchain technology and committed to fostering community engagement, we want to hear from you!

results.title: Define compliance metrics and checkpoints across stages | Gainsight Community
results.content: * Ensure compliance and visibility across journey stages. * Define compliance metrics and checkpoints across stages. # Define compliance metrics and checkpoints across stages. Ensuring a consistent customer journey requires well-defined compliance metrics that measure progress and engagement at each stage. By setting up compliance checkpoints across the lifecycle, your team can identify deviations early and ensure customers receive the right support to keep them on track. This article will guide you through defining compliance metrics and establishing checkpoints that align with each lifecycle stage, providing a clear structure for journey compliance. **Step 1: Identify Compliance Metrics for Each Stage**. Start by defining the specific metrics that indicate compliance for each stage of the customer journey, ensuring that progress is measurable and actionable. * **Feature Usage and Adoption**: In the Adoption stage, track feature engagement to confirm that customers are actively using core functionalities. **Step 2: Define Compliance Checkpoints for Each Lifecycle Stage**. Once metrics are defined, set specific checkpoints that indicate whether customers are meeting the compliance criteria for each stage. * **Onboarding Checkpoints**: Establish onboarding milestones, such as account setup, initial training, and first product use, to ensure customers are progressing smoothly. Use **Journey Orchestrator** to create automated reminders that encourage customers to complete each onboarding step​. Track these milestones in **Scorecards** to ensure customers are effectively adopting the product​. Use **Dashboards** to track whether these checkpoints are met as customers approach renewal​. Documenting compliance standards ensures that each team member understands what constitutes compliance at each stage and how to track it. * **Create a Compliance Standards Document**: Develop a document that outlines each compliance metric and checkpoint for every lifecycle stage, providing clear guidelines for your team. * **Use Scorecards to Track Compliance Status**: Configure **Scorecards** to visually indicate compliance status, such as “On Track,” “At Risk,” or “Non-Compliant.” This helps CSMs quickly identify customers who need additional support to stay on course​. * **Log Compliance Actions in Timeline**: Use **Timeline** to document compliance actions, such as completing a milestone or addressing a compliance gap. With compliance metrics and checkpoints in place, your team can begin tracking customer progress more effectively across each stage.
